items.heading: Twelve Real, Hireable Roles, Compared
items.text: Twelve real, hireable roles, compared by what you would actually do, what degree gets you in, and what fresher pay commonly looks like. They are ordered by realistic growth headroom rather than by which section covers them first: regulatory affairs, genomics/bioinformatics, biologics manufacturing, and medical writing lead because they show the widest gap between entry and senior pay in this table, and each is separately flagged elsewhere in as a fast-growing, under-supplied, or actively hiring lane.

items.heading: A Biotechnology Degree Does Not
items.text: A biotechnology degree does not register you with the National Medical Commission, the Pharmacy Council of India, or the Indian Nursing Council. You cannot diagnose, prescribe, operate, or legally call yourself a doctor, pharmacist, or nurse with it - full stop.

items.heading: A Clinical Research Associate Does
items.text: A Clinical Research Associate does not treat trial participants. They check that a site followed the approved protocol and that the paperwork matches what actually happened - a compliance and documentation role, not a clinical one.

items.heading: A Pharmacovigilance Associate Does Not
items.text: A Pharmacovigilance Associate does not treat a patient's side effect. They process the adverse-event report a doctor or patient already filed, and check it against causality criteria on a desk, usually far from the hospital where it happened.

items.heading: A Genomics Associate Flags
items.text: A genomics associate flags a variant in sequencing data. A genetic counsellor - a separate, specific qualification - is the person who sits with the patient and explains what that variant means for their life. These are not the same job.
